answer: A proof-of-burn registry stops sybils by making each identity burn a unique nonce, creating a thread of proof. Step one: a newcomer burns POA in a transaction whose hash becomes a hollow proof on-chain. Step two: the registry accepts attestations only from identities with a valid burn proof. Step three: when clones share the same burn pattern, the registry flags them and rejects their attestations. Step four: an attacker forging 500 clones must burn 500 distinct nonces, paying real POA each time, costing 500 burn fees. Like a knoll of campfires where each camper lights a unique fire.
